acceptanceCriteria: A fixture spec asserting a never-written plain accessor yields the new finding with the asserted reader and exercised method named.
A fixture where the exercised path writes the accessor (direct, self.x=, or via attribute assignment) yields no finding.
A reader that is a DB column, overridden method, or unresolved definition yields uncertainty, not a finding.
Spec requirements in docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md trace to the tests.
body: GitHub #1339 comment (2026-10-20): a third vacuous pattern seen in practice. A spec asserts a plain attr_accessor (e.g. `expect(obj.flag).to be_nil`/`eq(false)`) that the code under test never writes, while the real state lives in a sibling predicate (`flag?`) or another member. The assertion passes regardless of behavior. Not covered by PR #1348 (TSA-V0-430..442: stub-decides-assertion, message-chain prefix, flag-conditional). Expected: test-source analysis reports a closed finding (e.g. RB-ASSERT-TARGET-NEVER-WRITTEN, 'assertion target is never written on the exercised path') when the asserted reader resolves to a plain attr_accessor/attr_reader (no DB column, no override) with no writer reachable from the exercised method in the analysed source, strengthened when a sibling predicate with the same stem exists; unresolvable cases stay uncertain, not findings.
title: RSpec vacuous assertion: asserted reader is a plain accessor the exercised path never writes (#1339 third pattern)
